question: According to Le Canard Enchaîné1, the French agency responsible for monitoring and protecting against foreign digital interference has identified a number of Israeli manipulation and digital influence campaigns targeting candidates from La France Insoumise in Marseille, Toulouse and Roubaix during the 2026 local elections.

Although this foreign interference in European electoral processes poses as great a threat to the integrity of our democracies as Russian interference does, the Commission is turning a blind eye to the matter. However, the credibility of our policies depends on consistent responses.

Furthermore, despite the rise in such interference, the 2025 report of the Special Committee on the European Democratic Shield highlighted the failure to make use of the tools provided by the Digital Services Act, as well as their insufficient use during election campaigns. In this regard: 1.

Does the Commission intend to comment on this influence operation identified by the French intelligence services, as it has done in relation to other instances of interference targeting Member States?
Does it consider that such interference is compatible with the principles underpinning the EU-Israel Association Agreement?
How does it intend to safeguard the integrity of our electoral processes, given the shortcomings of the Digital Services Act identified by the Special Committee?
